finding: 2.1 (LinearSVC) was selected by validation F1=0.9065. Its final test F1=0.8965 and test AUC=0.9619.
For checking only, the highest test F1 was 2.1 (LinearSVC) with test F1=0.8965. The report should still say models were chosen by validation F1.
1.6 was the best NB setup by validation F1=0.8761; its final test F1=0.8649.
Raw text test F1=0.7990 vs cleaned text test F1=0.8009. Basic cleaning had only a small effect because BoW still sees similar key words.
With stopword removal test F1=0.8083 vs cleaned text test F1=0.8009. This checks whether common words add noise for NB.
Alpha was tuned on the validation set. The alpha_tuning_curve.png file shows which alpha gave the best validation F1.
BoW test F1=0.8009 vs TF-IDF test F1=0.8176. TF-IDF can help because it reduces the weight of very common words.
Unigram test F1=0.8176 vs unigram+bigram test F1=0.8649. Bigrams can capture short phrases such as 'not good'.
Best NB test F1=0.8649, LinearSVC test F1=0.8965, and Logistic Regression test F1=0.8888. This compares generative and discriminative classifiers using the same feature setting.
SBERT+LR test F1=0.8095 and SBERT+RBF SVC test F1=0.8022. SBERT is more modern, but it may not beat TF-IDF on long IMDb reviews without fine-tuning.
NB is fastest; LinearSVC and Logistic Regression take longer; SBERT needs an embedding step before classification. The training_time_comparison.png chart supports this point.
The error-analysis table checks difficult wrong predictions, including negation, mixed sentiment, sarcasm, and implicit sentiment.
